Analysis: Both hypotheses aim to elucidate mechanisms driving NAFLD, but they differ in approach. Hypothesis 1 leverages the modulation of hepatic oxidative stress through dietary antioxidants to rebalance PPAR isoforms. Its advantage lies in leaning on relatively established roles of oxidative stress and PPAR activity, making it more plausible and readily testable using defined antioxidant interventions. While it has some gaps in mechanistic detail and specificity, it remains within a well-understood metabolic framework and implies minimal safety risks. In contrast, Hypothesis 2 introduces a novel inter-organ communication mechanism involving the lipid mediator PC (18:0/18:1) and its effects on muscle PPARα. Although highly innovative, this hypothesis is more speculative with less established mechanistic support and faces greater challenges in experimental validation given the complexity of cross-tissue signaling. Overall, the clearer causal framework, higher plausibility, and more straightforward testability of Hypothesis 1 make it the superior choice.
